synopsis: Mississippi State University is identified as the source of MAVS, an open off-road simulator described across the virtual-job-site and sensor-simulation chapters [f3786, f4508]. MAVS automatically generates terrain with controllable roughness, ecosystem, haze and moonlight [f3786]. Its ray-traced lidar, camera and radar interact with rain, dust, fog and snow, extending its described capabilities from environment creation to sensor simulation [f4508]. The military and general off-road examples associate MAVS with both Mississippi State University and ERDC, but the supplied facts do not specify their respective organizational roles [f4159].

relations.note: Adds controllable terrain generation to the description of MAVS's off-road simulation capabilities.
Adds ERDC association and military and general off-road application contexts.
